meta.title: Ch 8: Other Indian Accounting Standards — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 8 (Other Indian Accounting Standards).

questions.q: A government grants a tax incentive that reduces the entity's current tax bill permanently for ten years on new units. Under Ind AS 20, this is:
o: A government grant recognised as deferred income
Not within the scope of Ind AS 20 as a grant — such tax benefits are addressed through Ind AS 12
A loan at a below-market rate
questions.why: Ind AS 20 explicitly excludes forms of government support that cannot be usefully separated from the entity's ordinary activities, e.g., tax incentives — benefits arising from tax exemptions/reliefs are dealt with under Ind AS 12 (deferral) rather than as 'grants'.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — scope exclusions are the standard ICAI 'which is NOT a grant' question AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Grants = transfers of ASSETS (cash, land). Tax breaks are not transfers — route them to Ind AS 12.

questions.q: A dairy's milch animals are reared by the entity for milk production. Under Ind AS 41/16, the animals themselves are:
o: Biological assets at fair value less costs to sell
Property, plant and equipment under the cost model
Intangible assets of the milk brand
questions.why: Bearer plants and bearer animals used in agriculture produce (milk-producing animals in ICAI's position: bearer animals follow PPE/Ind AS 16 treatment for the animals producing agri-produce over periods; the PRODUCE (milk) at the point of separation is Ind AS 41 at FVLCS). Note ICAI aligns bearer biological assets to Ind AS 16 while immature/produce remain Ind AS 41.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — bearer-vs-produce boundary is exactly the new-syllabus flavour AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Bearer = factory (PPE/16); produce = output (41 fair value). Once milk leaves the udder, 41 owns it.

questions.q: A government conveys land at a nominal price to a manufacturer as an incentive. Ind AS 20 allows measuring the grant at:
o: Fair value of the land, or the nominal amount with appropriate disclosure
questions.why: Ind AS 20: where free/nominal-consideration assets are received, measure at fair value (grant income over expected useful life) or, when fair value cannot be measured reliably, at the nominal amount.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — either-or measurement is the phrasing ICAI uses Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Free land, real numbers: fair value if it can be had; a symbolic 1-rupee entry with disclosure if not.

questions.q: Tax exemptions received as part of the government's general fiscal policy available to all qualifying taxpayers are:
o: Not grants — outside Ind AS 20 scope as they are not transfers of resources from government
questions.why: Forms of government assistance benefiting via tax determination (exemptions/rebates) cannot be differentiated from ordinary trading activity for Ind AS 20 — generally outside 'grant' treatment; recognised under Ind AS 12 mechanics where relevant.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the scope-boundary is asked via 'which is a grant' format Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Grants = transfers TO you outside the tax calculation; tax breaks = the tax calculation itself.

questions.q: Biological produce attached to a bearer biological asset at the point of harvest is measured:
o: Fair value less costs to sell
questions.why: Harvested produce = Ind AS 41 at FVLCS; bearer assets follow Ind AS 16 once mature. Gains/losses on FVLCS change go to P&L.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the bearer/produce split is Ind AS 41's hot zone AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Trees are PPE after maturity; fruit is fair-value produce from the branch onward.

questions.q: A government subscribing to equity shares on the same terms as other investors is:
questions.why: Government participating as an owner on equal terms = equity, not Ind AS 20 grant; concessions in price vs market may create grant-like elements.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the equal-terms exclusion Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Same terms as shareholders? It's ownership, not subsidy.

questions.topic: Ind AS 102 — scope of employee definition
questions.q: Ind AS 102 applies to SBP with non-employees when:
o: The goods/services received relate to consumption for the entity in an employee-like arrangement/fair value not reliably measurable
questions.why: For non-employee SBP, the presumption of reliability of the goods/services FV can be rebutted in exceptional cases — measurement date then becomes when goods/services received.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the exceptional-measurement-date twist Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 102 — scope of employee definition
mem.tip: With outsiders, value the work; if that's unmeasurable, the options themselves at receipt day.

questions.q: A non-monetary government grant is measured at:
o: Fair value of the asset received
questions.why: Ind AS 20: non-monetary grants recorded at FV of the asset (or nominal amount where FV cannot be measured).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — measurement-basis recall Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Value what you were gifted like a purchase; if impossible, the one-rupee note with disclosure.

questions.q: A jewellery retailer's identical-looking high-value stones are best costed by:
questions.why: Ind AS 2: items that are not ordinarily interchangeable and goods produced for specific projects are accounted for by SPECIFIC identification — generic pooling would misstate each stone's margin.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — formula follows the item's interchangeability, not convenience AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: A qualifying asset funded partly from general borrowings capitalises interest using:
o: The general borrowing capitalisation rate applied to expenditure exceeding specific borrowings
Actual rate on the whole borrowing
questions.why: For general borrowings: capitalise at the weighted average rate applicable to borrowings outstanding during the period, applied to the asset expenditure EXCEEDING specific borrowings.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — specific loans use their own rate; general pools use the blend AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Pool money borrows a pooled cost.

questions.q: Capitalisation of borrowing costs PAUSES when:
o: Active development of the asset is interrupted for a substantial period
questions.why: Capitalisation suspends while active development stops (substantial interruptions); routine temporary delays do not pause it; it ceases when the asset is ready for its intended use or sale.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the pause button is the worksite, not the lender AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Work stop, cost stop — capitalisation follows the crane, not the clock.

questions.q: A grant for setting up a plant in a notified region may be presented as:
o: Either deferred income or by deducting the grant from the asset's carrying amount
questions.why: Ind AS 20 permits both presentations (deferred income released over the useful life, or netted against the asset reducing depreciation) — consistency of policy and liability treatment when repayment becomes probable are the tested nuances.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — two presentations, one chosen policy AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The gift can sit beside the asset or inside it — never in both at once.

questions.q: Bearer plants (e.g., a rubber tree) are accounted for as:
o: Biological assets at fair value less costs to sell
Property, plant and equipment under Ind AS 16, while the produce on them is at fair value less costs to sell
questions.why: The PRODUCING plant is PP&E (depreciated once at maturity); only the PRODUCE (latex, fruit on the tree) is fair-valued until harvest — holding that split is the whole test.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the bearer is PP&E; the borne is harvest AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The tree is the machine; the sap is the stock.

questions.q: A cyclone loss in the current year is presented in the statement of profit and loss as:
o: A separate 'extraordinary items' line below tax
Within ordinary activities — extraordinary captions are prohibited, with separate disclosure of nature and amount if material
questions.why: Ind AS 1 PROHIBITS labelling anything extraordinary; large one-offs stay inside continuing operations (other income/expense) with separate disclosure where needed for a fair view.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — no extraordinary line — only extra disclosure Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

questions.q: A dividend to shareholders is recognised as a liability when:
o: The board proposes it for the year
Approved by the shareholders (where approval is required) before the reporting period ends
Declared after the reporting period ends
questions.why: Proposed dividends are not a liability at the year end; where shareholder approval is required the obligation arises on approval — post-year-end declarations are disclosed, not recognised.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — proposal promises nothing; approval obliges Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A wish becomes a wallet only past the vote.

questions.q: Development spend is capitalised as an intangible only when:
o: Technical feasibility, intention to complete, ability to use or sell, probable future economic benefits, adequate resources, and reliable measurement are ALL demonstrated
questions.why: Research is ALWAYS expensed; development capitalises only through all six Ind AS 38 gates — one failed gate sends the spend to P&L.

questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — six keys for one door Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: A plan becomes an asset when it can rent its own room.
